clue.text: Removes cover and prepares to receive deliveries

definitions.meaning: to take off a guard, a protective cover, from something
in cricket a batsman marks his position at the crease before facing the bowler's deliveries

explanation.surface: Someone strips off a dust sheet and gets ready for the parcels to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests the post, but they are balls bowled in cricket, where a batsman marks his stance before facing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally lifting off a protective guard, and the cricketing ritual of a batsman setting his stance at the crease.

clue.text: A maiden-and a possible name for her?

parts.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what name might suit a young unmarried woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden, an over with no runs scored, is written M.
explanation.definitionFit: Amanda is a girl's forename, so it is one name a young woman might have.

clue.text: Explanation for mislaying of six geese

indicators.note: mislaying suggests putting things in the wrong place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone accounts for losing half a dozen farmyard birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Exegesis is critical interpretation, especially of scripture or a text.

clue.text: Enormous sort of car for a Chinese native

parts.note: giant means huge
a panda car is a British police patrol car, once painted in blue and white

explanation.surface: A huge vehicle is supplied for a resident of China.
explanation.walkthrough: A panda car is the British nickname for a small police patrol car.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is a black-and-white bear found only in the mountains of China.

clue.text: Dancing girl mostly supportive of Jack's rebellious son

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: a jack or jack tar is a sailor, and AB is an able seaman

indicators.note: mostly means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: Salome danced for Herod and asked for the head of John the Baptist

explanation.surface: A dancer props up a sailor's wayward boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supportive of' puts SALOM (SALOME less its last letter, by 'mostly') under AB.
explanation.definitionFit: Absalom was the son of King David who led a revolt against his father.

clue.text: Pipeline put under water, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the clue word's sound, not its spelling, gives the entry

parts.note: to duck someone is to push them briefly under water

explanation.surface: A conduit was laid beneath the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A duct is a tube or channel carrying fluid, air or cable.

clue.text: Roman force I hit hard, as sacker of Rome

parts.note: vis is the Latin word for force
got is used for struck, as in a stone got him on the head
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A Roman soldier strikes forcefully as the city is plundered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman force' suggests a legion, but it is the Latin word for force.
explanation.definitionFit: The Visigoths under Alaric plundered the city in AD 410.

clue.text: Torture for diminutive general's men

parts.note: General Tom Thumb was the stage name of the tiny showman Charles Stratton
a crew is a team of men

explanation.surface: A small commander's troops face cruel punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'diminutive general' is P. T. Barnum's famous midget performer, General Tom Thumb.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval device for crushing the digits to extract confessions, so an instrument of torment.

clue.text: Showing arrogance in high position, with contemptuous expression

parts.note: up means raised or aloft
pish is an old exclamation of scorn or impatience

explanation.surface: A haughty person stands on high and sneers.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppish is a British informal word for self-important or presumptuous behaviour.

clue.text: Writer creating leading characters in new serial

indicators.note: new signals that these letters are formed into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the first two letters of the alphabet are A and B
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author introduces the main figures of a fresh serial story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading characters' looks like the heroes of the serial, but it is the alphabet's opening letters AB, shuffled with SERIAL by 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: François Rabelais was the French Renaissance author of Gargantua and Pantagruel.

clue.text: Consideration for others — a Liberal platitude

parts.note: a truism is a trite, self-evident statement

explanation.surface: Caring for others is dismissed as a woolly Liberal cliché.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruism is unselfish concern for the welfare of other people.

clue.text: TNT is in these detonators

definitions.meaning: the letters TNT are written in capital letters
small explosive percussion charges that set off a larger blast, as in a toy gun

explanation.surface: An explosive is packed into the firing devices.
explanation.walkthrough: TNT seems to be the explosive, but the first sense is typographic: the letters are printed in capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper-case letters, and small percussion charges used to fire explosives or toy pistols.

clue.text: Fill gap in bouquet, say

indicators.note: say means the spoken word, not the written one, gives the entry

parts.note: a bouquet is praise or a compliment, as in bouquets and brickbats

explanation.surface: Someone tucks an extra flower into a gap in the posy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' suggests flowers, but it means a word of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To complement is to complete or make whole, supplying what is lacking.

clue.text: Rich Milanese noble goes to America

parts.note: Prospero is the deposed Duke of Milan in Shakespeare's The Tempest
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A wealthy Italian aristocrat emigrates to the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosperous means wealthy and successful, a close synonym.

clue.text: Fly over land that's constantly burning

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece placed over another comes first

parts.note: to pilot is to fly an aircraft
to light is to come down or settle, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: An aircraft passes above a country ablaze without pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' and 'land' look like a flight plan; both are verbs giving the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flame kept burning permanently in a gas appliance to ignite the main burner.

clue.text: Disorder in a Mediterranean port

parts.note: a mess is a state of untidiness or confusion
taken as written

explanation.surface: Chaos reigns in a harbour town on the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Messina is a port city in Sicily facing the Italian mainland across its strait.

clue.text: Basic equestrian ability achieved by vast majority

definitions.meaning: a rider's secure position in the saddle
a parliamentary constituency won by a huge margin and unlikely to change hands

explanation.surface: A rider's sound grounding wins overwhelming approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider's firm position on horseback, and a constituency held by a large majority at an election.

clue.text: Shoemaker's work on side of Wellington

definitions.meaning: a kind of laced half-boot or shoe
the Prussian field marshal who was Wellington's ally at Waterloo in 1815

explanation.surface: A cobbler finishes the side of a rubber boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wellington' suggests the rubber boot, chiming with the shoemaker, but here it is the Duke, whose Prussian ally at Waterloo lent his name to a style of shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A laced shoe named after Field Marshal Blücher, the Prussian commander who fought alongside Wellington at Waterloo.

clue.text: Libertine chaps, to begin with, like a heavenly body

indicators.note: to begin with means only the opening letter of the word is used

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
a nova is a star that suddenly flares in brightness

explanation.surface: A rake's men begin to resemble a star.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Casanova was the Venetian adventurer whose name became a byword for a womaniser.

clue.text: Frolic in "Blithe Spirit"

definitions.meaning: Shelley's ode to this songbird opens 'Hail to thee, blithe Spirit!'

explanation.surface: Someone romps about in a production of Noël Coward's comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks suggest Coward's play, but the line is from Shelley's ode addressed to a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for playing pranks, and the bird hailed as a carefree spirit in Shelley's poem.

clue.text: Mae West's biography found in this?

definitions.text: Mae West's biography found in this?

parts.words: Mae West's biography found in this?
parts.note: a Mae West is RAF slang for an inflatable vest worn over the chest; read playfully, a biography of the actress would be enclosed in its book cover

explanation.surface: A reader wonders where to find the life story of the Hollywood star.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mae West was wartime slang for an airman's inflatable vest, named after the actress's figure; the clue reads the answer as the cover wrapped round a biography.
explanation.definitionFit: A buoyancy vest was nicknamed a Mae West, and a book's life story wears a dust cover.

clue.text: Name Lawrence acquired as author

definitions.meaning: T. E. Lawrence of Arabia enlisted in the RAF and Tank Corps under the assumed surname ...

explanation.surface: A writer took on a new name when he became famous.
explanation.definitionFit: The alias adopted by Lawrence of Arabia, and the surname of the Irish dramatist of Pygmalion.

clue.text: Engaged in sailing manoeuvre in storm

parts.note: at means busy with, as in at work
to tack is to turn a boat's bow through the wind

explanation.surface: A crew is busy changing course during a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm' looks like weather to sail in, but it is a verb, to assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a place is to assault it violently.

clue.text: Action halted as cold wind engulfs one

indicators.note: engulfs means the wind's letters swallow and surround the letter for one

parts.note: the mistral is a cold northerly wind of southern France
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A freezing gale swallows someone and brings activity to a stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Action' is a legal action, a lawsuit, and 'halted' a trial abandoned before verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action stopped because of a procedural error or a hung jury is declared void.

clue.text: The same endless newspapers turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the letters read from bottom to top
endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the press are collectively the media

explanation.surface: The same old papers keep appearing without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts MEDIA to MEDI, which 'turned up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Idem is Latin for the same, used in citations to repeat a previous reference.

clue.text: Not a well-earned degree

parts.note: read as 'not earned while well': a pass granted to a student too ill to sit the examinations

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at an undeserved university qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-earned' wants to mean deserved, but split it as earned while well: the degree goes to a student who was sick at exam time.
explanation.definitionFit: From Latin for 'he is sick', a British university degree awarded to a candidate prevented by illness from sitting finals.

clue.text: Graduation from new university with a new church

parts.note: N is again the abbreviation for new
N is again the abbreviation for new
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A ceremony at a newly founded university also takes place in a new church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graduation' suggests a degree ceremony, but it means a fine gradation of shade or meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle shade or step of difference, a gradation.

clue.text: Go to work on the railway

definitions.meaning: literally, to build the lines trains run on

explanation.surface: Someone sets off to a job laying lines for the trains.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for leaving promptly, and literally laying the rails a train runs on.
